conventions.convention: Response sets are finite and nonempty. EOS ends the sampled prefix; exhausting the positive token budget appends an unsampled truncation marker.
Policy masses are totally differentiable on an open parameter domain, positive on a fixed nonempty support and zero outside it. Scores are defined only on the support.

Correctness C and verifier acceptance A are distinct supplied binary predicates. Rejection returns the first accepted sample; best-of-N maximizes the supplied score and resolves ties by the least response in a supplied strict total order.

Group standard deviation uses divisor G. A zero standard deviation sets all advantages to zero. Samples, rewards and advantages remain frozen during inner updates; the ratio is sequence-level and the penalty is exact forward KL.

Sampling and exact evaluations are supplied terminating operations. The update additionally receives total exact gradient-decision and domain-membership oracles; their internal costs have no asserted uniform bound.

The group-centering identities concern unnormalized rewards and independent draws from the same policy, with G ≥ 2. They do not assert unbiasedness after random standardization, clipping or old-policy sample reuse.

load_bearing.statement: For each prompt, a finite response law has totally differentiable normalized masses on a fixed nonempty support, with separate supplied correctness and verifier predicates, finite rewards and selection scores, and a deterministic strict total tie order.

For every parameter in the open domain of the finite fixed-support policy and every fixed finite reward r, the expected score is zero and the expected reward-weighted score equals the gradient of J, where J is the finite expected reward.

With a perfect verifier and N independent draws of correctness probability p, rejection succeeds with probability 1−(1−p)^N. If every candidate has false-acceptance probability at most ε, any verifier-accepted output selected from the N candidates is incorrect with probability at most Nε, without independence. Adaptive conditional correctness probability at least p on every positive-probability no-success history bounds total failure by (1−p)^N.

The finite procedure freezes old-policy groups and normalized advantages, uses a clipped sequence-ratio objective with exact forward KL, and applies supplied gradient-oracle updates only when the domain oracle accepts; it returns complete, undefined-gradient or invalid-update.
For G ≥ 2 independent same-policy responses, E[G⁻¹ Σᵢ(Rᵢ−R̄)Sᵢ | q] = (1−1/G)∇J. Replacing R̄ by the leave-one-out mean makes the expectation ∇J.
For probability masses p,q on an enumerated finite nonempty set, with p(y)>0 implying q(y)>0, define ρ=p/q where q>0 and ρ=0 otherwise. For every real-valued f, Σqρf=Σpf; in particular Σqρ=1.

concerns.concern: Facts & Assumptions says “Pr(C(c)=1)=3/4” and “Pr(C(w)=1)=0”. Here C is a supplied deterministic predicate and c is explicitly correct, so C(c)=1 is certain. The intended assumption is Pr(Y=c)=3/4 and Pr(Y=w)=1/4, with C(c)=1 and C(w)=0. The Example and its numerical verification use that intended law correctly.

The opening paragraph defines verifier-selected accuracy as “the fraction correct among returned responses the verifier accepts” without addressing an empty accepted set. The protocol permits an always-rejecting verifier, so this denominator can be zero. State that the statistic is undefined when no response is accepted, or supply an explicit convention. The numerical example has positive acceptance probability and is unaffected.
